title: P300 dataset BI2014b from a "Brain Invaders" experiment
description: EEG recordings from 38 healthy participants playing in pairs the multi-user version of Brain Invaders, a visual P300-based brain-computer interface using the oddball paradigm on a grid of 36 symbols. Data were recorded with 32 wet electrodes per subject across three randomized conditions (Solo1, Solo2, Collaboration) at GIPSA-lab, Grenoble, in 2014. The dataset supports research on collaborative BCIs and inter-brain synchrony in hyperscanning.
methods_description: Pairs of participants played Brain Invaders 2 in three randomized conditions: Solo1, Solo2, and Collaboration. Each game session had 9 levels with predefined alien configurations, and a repetition consisted of 12 flashes of pseudo-random groups of 6 symbols. EEG was recorded at 512 Hz from 32 active wet Ag/AgCl electrodes per subject with g.USBamp amplifiers, referenced to the right earlobe with ground at Fz. Experimental tags were synchronized via a USB analog-to-digital converter. A real-time adaptive Riemannian minimum distance to mean classifier provided online feedback. In the solo conditions the non-playing participant watched a cross, which controls for fake inter-brain synchrony.
